text: All right, fire away. >> Uh, do you expect Kyler out there today? >> I don't. >> Is he going to play Sunday? >> Probably not. >> Any Is this With the Thursday game, does that play any role in >> Haven't even thought about it. >> Do you want to be telling what the injury is to his shoulder? >> Nope. >> I'm assuming counting on Guyton and Malik Muhammad are good to go. >> We'll see with the injury report coming out, guys. >> You guys have a first quarter success this this season so far, the way the offense got off to a hot start. They they do a great job bringing it to life there early in games and um you know, maybe it's just the comfort level now that a lot of these guys are second year in the system and uh and uh you know, that we we are starting out of the gate pretty hot um whether it's running or or throwing the ball. So um I think that's that's been a good thing to see and we need to continue to to have that happen going forward as well cuz uh you know, that's been a big part of of what we preach um and there's certainly other areas that we can uh get better at, but I I feel like every year there's always one section of the game, hey, we're not starting fast enough or we're coming out of the out of halftime slow or we're not finishing games the right way. Um I just don't feel that with this crew. I think we've all We've had some success really throughout the 60 minutes um you know, with throughout the season so far. It's been >> With that, New Orleans has been slow starting this season. How does that catch your attention when you feel like there is a decisive strength there? >> Yeah, well I mean all it takes is one game for that to flip form. I think more than anything it's just the awareness level for us at halftime that this team they've proven that they're a really good second half team and so regardless of what happens in the first half for us we're going to have to come out and and keep our foot on the gas there throughout the second half because it's for whatever reason they seem to get really hot. >> You were you talked about turnover margin earlier. I think your DBs have four interceptions all year. What sort of production do you need from them to maybe take advantage of the pressure that Jeffrey's helping you guys get? >> Yeah, well just take advantage of any opportunities that come our way. So we we are extremely ball conscious. I think our guys have done a great job throughout this week. We've kind of taken it to another level as a coaching staff. Our guys are aware of it and when those opportunities come our way just making sure we we capitalize on it. >> Take it to another level? >> Uh just continue to talk about it and keep those those coaching habits in house though. >> When you were talking the other day about the rushing efficiency, you were giving some specific numbers. What what are you referring to? How are you calculating how efficiently you guys are running? >> Yeah, I think might have talked we might have brought this up last year. I can't remember but regardless of run or pass an efficient play for us on first down is a third of the distance. So normally it's first and 10 so it's four more. Second down is half the distance. So depends on what second second and 10 you need five yards. Second and two you only need a one yard gain. And then third down or fourth down it's it's to convert. So it's a little bit predicated by by the distance with which you need to go. >> So when you say 50% rushing efficiency you're saying 50% of the time you're getting you're hitting those >> Correct. >> Along along those lines, you know, of what you said we just a few minutes ago, looking back at last year versus this year, what are some of the things that you would say have been successful, you've gained, where you're better off because of the, you know, what's led you to the record of seven and two? >> I I, yeah, I I honestly I haven't uh haven't compared a whole lot year to year yet. Um I'm sure we'll do that at the end of the year, but we we're doing a lot of really good things. Um the play style is the most important thing though. That's that's what you want to show up on tape. Um we pride ourselves in being a physical group. We we pride ourselves in being sound both schematically and with our fundamentals and then and then we pride ourselves in being a poised group as well. So um I I think those three elements do show up and I think the second half of the season we we got to sink into that and that's that's really what I want to see coming out of the bye week is us not just pick up where we left off, but really take it to the next level. >> And where where have you seen >> appreciative of your keeping him engaged and let have competition throughout the summer. Talk about What have you liked from how he handled that, the constant competition and push from from Aussie and then how he's played on the field so far? >> No, I mean I think all those guys, whether it was him or Braxton, Aussie, um everybody that we had uh in in the stable there trying to trying to get reps, they they did a great job taking it head on. They I I think we're very transparent in what we needed to see just consistency wise and um you know, he he's done a great job taking the the bull by the horns and and taking advantage of a situation where uh you know, we feel really positive about what he brings to the table in the running game. In the passing game he's grown tremendously from uh where he was when we first came in the building a year and a half ago and so the confidence level has has um just continued to to get higher and higher. I I noticed it from day one when he comes into a meeting, he he's constantly taking notes um whatever you say, and and I know that carries over to the defense, uh the D-line meetings as well. So I think everybody hears everything this day and age. Why is it important to you to be so straightforward about things that you guys are trying to fix? >> I don't know any other way. You know I just try to be truthful. >> Scientist in him. >> There you there you go. Yeah. I just try to be truthful. So [snorts] whatever you guys ask I try to give. >> Ben, what's next for uh in this stage of his comeback? Do you anticipate mixing him in more than he has the the previous few games? >> Potentially. Yeah yeah, you know it's you know coach Roschow brought it up earlier on this week that Tuesday practice went a long way, but we we need to see more of it. So, that's that was one good pad of practice. We we got to continue to [snorts] to bank those reps and and just show show that we're ready for more playing time. And it's like that with every guy and every position right now, you know. We got to each week's its own story and and just because you've done this or that doesn't mean that that's going to be your role going forward. So, he's continuing to earn that. >> All the every defensive player has talked about Jeffrey raising the floor on Do you see it the same with the offensive guys too? Like is there a level that he brings that gets more out of them in practice? >> I don't know that. I don't I don't know that quite yet. I certainly you feel his presence out there, you know. You hear him out there. And I I think that that is a good thing. It gives us a little bit of an edge as a team, no doubt. >> Thank you.

title: Actor David Corenswet: The Hardest Part about Playing Superman Is…? | The Rich Eisen Show
text: What was the toughest thing about playing Superman? Or for you, David? >> I mean, looking back, there're a lot of a lot of great challenges that came along with it. Gaining the weight for the first time in my life. Um uh the the wirework, the stuntwork was a a new thing for me that was wonderful and challenging. I think I I I think back to what Christopher Reeve said about his thoughts going into shooting the the original Superman the movie, which was, you know, ultimately, it's just you out there in the tights. [laughter] And nobody's coming to save you. And uh so sometimes the biggest challenge was just standing there for a scene uh in the tights in the trunks. [laughter] And and somehow finding a way to to not feel silly. Um and not try too hard to make up for it in some way. Not not act too tough or or or shy away from what it is. I think it's one of the great things about the character is that he he's proud to be the big red and blue. And uh and he'll just stand there in his trunks and uh maybe you'll laugh at him, but he'll be happy to have made you laugh. >> David, I mean, it's not like you're strolling down Hollywood Boulevard here. You know what I mean? >> That's true. That's the other guy. >> like you're not going through Times Square dressed like this guy. Like you are playing Superman. Like you are This is the real thing. >> Yeah. >> So but you still felt standing around like >> yeah. >> silly? Really? >> It was really nice anytime somebody I would walk up to somebody and they'd go like, oh my god, it's Superman. I go, okay, I'm going to take that with me for the next few minutes and hopefully that'll keep my confidence up just long [laughter] enough to get through the next next scene. Especially when you're standing across from from Rachel Brosnahan who's dressed all cool and she looks so beautiful and she's so sharp and and Nicholas Hoult in his cool tailored suits and then his war suit in this movie we just shot. He's got his big green war suit. >> Like why can't I get some armor? >> [laughter] >> Well, I'll be straight up with you, okay? I'm a happily married man of 23 years, but if I were across from Rachel Brosnahan, I want to be dressed as Superman. [laughter] >> Yeah, sure. >> That, that would be >> There would be worst worst ways to be dressed across from her. >> That's what I'm saying. Like I'd rather I'd rather be dressed as that than say what I'm wearing today. >> you'd be wearing short shorts in a in a 80s cutoff. >> That would not look good for me. [laughter] Either way, I would look like Parsons in the Superman. That's my problem. You've got you've got what you got going for you. Uh what's your favorite scene from the Superman movie where you where you like that's the one that I'm I'm psyched that I was Superman in this scene. >> Um I love the interview scene uh with Rachel. That was such a fun scene to shoot. It was the first scene that we shot. It was two days and it was like shooting a movie uh shooting like a 1950s Cary Grant, you know, movie. Just the dialogue, quippy and funny and just about these characters. Um there were so many great action pieces. Actually, in this movie and the next Superman movie that that we finished this summer, there are some uh incredible new uh flying and and fights. They they uh they really up their game there. So in some ways those are the ones I I'm really excited for people to see those cuz um those are are those were a lot of fun to shoot and I think will end up being a lot of fun to do. >> Okay. >> It's kind of the same with with a movie like this. Like some of the football stuff was the most fun. When I gave and took my first hits, I didn't play contact sports growing up. So this movie was the first time I ever got hit by a guy or got to hit a guy. >> Even in Superman you did that? >> Well, no, I I'm throwing punches, but it's all it's a little more choreographed for the superhero stuff. Like I guess yeah, I got tackled a couple times, but in this movie it's we're in shoulder pads and we're we're going for it. Um >> when so in the scene where Lawrence Taylor is knocking you down? >> That's me some of the time. I [laughter] don't want to give too much away, but but a couple of those are me. Um I got to give credit to my football double Jacob who who took the really gnarly hits and he was amazing. But um >> [clears throat] >> okay, took the hits. >> Um but then in the then you've also got like, you know, it's a football movie, all these great football scenes, kickoff coverage, the running in slow motion, all that stuff is awesome. And then some of the scenes with Michael and Isabelle where we're just going at each other or uh or the more intimate scenes where it gets a little more emotional and you're you're really digging into the characters. With two great actors like that and our whole cast is so wonderful. Um watching the movie, those are the those are the scenes that make me think back to what it felt like making it. >> Well, again, I think Isabelle is coming on our show when we go to New York. title: Steelers Breakdown w/ No Huddle Eagles LIVE
text: With you all as always.  And that man is Johnny McGonigal.  If you read Penn Live, if you know our coverage of the Eagles, Johnny is our Eagles writer.  And this is a really fun week for us because we get to collaborate together. Johnny, you and I usually only do this for the draft, or for some other things when we 're both in the owners' meetings. But this is really fun, actually , that we can do this. Corporate synergy, right, Nick?  Yes , it's great, you know, for the Steelers Breakdown and the No Huddle show. If there are any fans of both teams out there, maybe a divided household, you know those exist all over Pennsylvania, where you have a Steelers fan on one side and an Eagles fan on the other. They should subscribe to both, Steelers Breakdown and the No Huddle show. This is incredible, man.  This is great .  I'm really looking forward to starting. This is, this is great.  And the Steelers and Eagles renew their state rivalry this week, which has really been felt, it feels like it's been played a lot more in recent years because of the new seventeenth game rule, these two teams have ended up facing each other.  NFC East has appeared.  And the Steelers and the Eagles have had a really interesting history.  The Steelers haven't won in Philadelphia since 1965. That's an impressive statistic to think about. Meanwhile, the Eagles are fielding probably their worst team in a very, very long time.  So I guess we'll start here .   Let 's start with the Eagles.  Give me a summary of this American football team .  Obviously everyone knows about injuries.  Hurts is out following the blood clot situation.  Saquon has lost playing time.  Devonta Smith lost playing time. Jordan Davis is no longer there.  You know, there are many different things.  Lane Johnson retired mid-season.   A lot has happened with this Eagles team to get to this point, basically out of contention for the playoffs this season. Yes, look, they're two and seven, with a streak of seven consecutive losses.   They just had their week off. The trade deadline came and went , and they made a great deal by sending Jordan Davis, so they got a first and second round pick; the value of that, I think they could have done it even if they were five and four. But it speaks volumes about where they are right now , switching to a young player who helped them win a Super Bowl two years ago and was named captain this offseason. He's a leader in the locker room, and the fact that they're willing to trade him tells you where they are this season, and I totally understand Howie Roseman's perspective because, you know, week after week he's seen this team. I've seen this team. Eagles fans have watched this team make the same mistakes over and over again without really improving much. For the most part, it's been the offensive this year.  We can analyze exactly why, but broadly speaking, the offense under Sean Mannion, which has certainly been plagued by injuries, has not been good enough at all. In fact, it's been quite bad.  And then the defense has been quite inconsistent, more inconsistent than you'd expect from Vic Fangio's unit .  So yes, week after week it has been tough for Eagles fans, many of whom have already shifted their attention to the draft, which is where we are right now at the halfway point of the season, which is surprising. It is.  I mean, I think everyone was pointing to them as the favorites in the NFC East thinking they would win, be back in the playoffs, and then a lot of things kept happening that caused it to plummet very quickly. In other words, if you had told an Eagles fan eight weeks ago that Joe Milton would be starting games for them, I think they would have called you crazy . Tanner McKee's experiment did not go well, of course. I find it interesting because I think this Eagles team is in a position where they can now quickly strengthen because of what Howie has done. But I also think that, wow, this year there are some "what happened here ?" moments with the team's construction, the fact of the offensive line.   I mean, yesterday I saw some footage about this team.   I've never seen an Eagles offensive line in the last decade play the way this team does. Um, they're having problems at the front. The Steelers should be full of opportunities, even if Nick Herbig doesn't play in this game, with guys like Highsmith, Watt, Hayward, and Benton to get the job done. Um, but tell me about the offense. Why isn't it working?  I think everyone knows, listen, Joe Milton doesn't know where the ball is going half the time Um, run towards some captures.  There are many different things about Joe Milton himself, but there's no ground game to talk about.  Saquon doesn't look totally like Saquon. Um, it seems he's still dealing with hamstring issues. Hm, tell me about this, because I think everyone could say, oh, they're missing Wicks , they're missing Smith, and that's part of it .  And yes, of course it is, but it's not everything It's clear that there are more problems than just injuries. Yes, look.  So, starting with Joe Milton, um, just a quick little story that, you know, Steelers or Pittsburgh fans might find amusing. Before that game against the Giants before the bye week where he made his first start with the Eagles, the last time I saw him play in person was when he played for Tennessee I was covering Pitt for the Pittsburgh Post Gazette and was down at Neland Stadium. Joe Milton started in that game. He missed about three touchdown passes before getting injured, and then Hendon Hooker came in and almost pulled off a comeback.  Pitt and Kenny Pickett end up winning that game.  But I remember being in the press box at the Neland Stadium thinking : this guy has a cannon arm.   He simply can't, he can't throw to wide-open receivers.  And, well , that's one reason why he's not one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL.  It's their precision.  I mean, he has the arm, he has the mobility, but the pocket awareness isn't really there, and certainly the precision isn't there. But he wasn't the problem in the game against the Giants, and really, Tanner McKee was the problem because of how inconsistent he played and because he didn't impress anyone.  That's why they benched him and he's on an expiring contract, so they have no obligation to him as a substitute But he wasn't even entirely the problem. Against the Commanders, you know, last week, a defense that does n't really inspire anyone sacked him five times, and yeah, is Tanner McKee a little static back there? Clear. Um, but it's because the offensive line can't block anyone and it's been like that all season. Even when Jalen Hurts was there as quarterback, think back to week one and week two against the Commanders and the Titans, games they won by a narrow margin and ultimately against bad teams. It's because Jalen Hurts put on that Superman cape and said, hey, I'm going to win the game for us in the end. Um, not to mention the fact that he's running for his life behind an offensive line that has really deteriorated. Lane Johnson obviously retired before that game against the Rams in week four. Uh, but even before that, you know , Landon Dickerson goes on the injured list after week one, following a preseason where we heard he was healthy after not being healthy last year. That prompted Cam Jurgens to switch from center to left guard. Well, Jurgens isn't a guard.  He wasn't a good centre last year either, and he wasn't good in week one as a centre.   They ended up trading him to the Ravens and getting a second- round pick, which is credit to Howie Roseman again; how they got a second-round pick for him, I have no idea. But with all that going on, you have a 2025 fifth-round pick, Drew Kendall, at center. At one point, you had Willie Lampkin at left guard, you know, an undrafted guy in 2025 while Landon Dickerson was out. Dickerson has returned, but he hasn't looked good at all due to all those injuries.  Jordan Mailata continues to play well as a left tackle. Tyler Steen has always been just an average lineman as a right guard.  And then, because Lane Johnson retired, you have a third- round rookie, Markell Bell, at right tackle, and speaking of this matchup, that's a duel to watch at right tackle against the pass rushers, particularly TJ Watt. But Markell Bell has had its ups and downs.   They did n't expect him to play important matches this year.  He has been asked to be an anchor on the right side and that has, unsurprisingly, been very up and down So, really, this offensive line that lost its legendary coach in the offseason, Jeff Stoutland, who had been with the Eagles for over a decade, had been the architect of those offensive lines that have been the foundation of this team's success for the last decade, really.   He left due to a disagreement about the future of the offensive and where they were taking it, hiring Sean McVay in a new system. They brought in Chris Cooper from the Vikings, who had somewhat inconsistent success there And really this offensive line just hasn't clicked after an offseason where we heard all those guys saying, "Hey, this system, this Shanahan and McVay system is going to be great for us."  It's going to be great for ground play. Saquon was excited and this offensive line really hasn't managed to solidify at all.   He has n't done it and it shows, and I was watching part of that game against the Giants and you just couldn't believe what you were seeing. Arvel Reese is a phenomenal talent, but the way they made it look easy to press him.   They simply let it slide in that capture.  They simply let it go completely.  You can't do that. The most unblocked pressures in the league, Nick.  The highest number of unblocked pressures in the league. Wow. The Steelers struggle to generate pressure without blocking, so I'm interested to see if Patrick Graham can do it. Much of the Steelers' pressure is simply them winning individual matchups. But they have had some good moments So this could be an interesting match for someone like Patrick Queen or Jalen Ramsey, who have both been playing very well.  Ramsey has had some plays that decided games.  He had the decisive play in Tampa Bay after a blitz from the edge, starting from the slot. PQ, Patrick Queen, has achieved a sack in three consecutive games. He has continued to play very well as a linebacker. In that sense, he's a great blitzer. So I'm interested to see how that develops. I'm interested to see how they play against the Steelers' defense. The Steelers' defense is obviously coming off its worst game of the year, but the question with them is: did they just run into a chainsaw named Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins?  And I think there's a lot of truth to that, because man, those guys dominated them all night and it did n't matter what they did. They play a lot of zone coverage.  The Steelers don't really tend to play man-to-man much.  Asante Samuel Jr. had difficulties on one side.  Darnell Dean has played well for the other.  But they are a team that likes to play zonal defense. But this Eagles offense is exactly the type of offense that the Steelers' defense has been good against this year.  I think about the games against Jayden Daniels, Cooper Rush, and even Daniel Jones, and they've been able to really shut down those teams. Tell me what you think about this defense, because I know I found that interesting.   I 've watched the Eagles' defense a bit this year and they still seem to be decent. There are good players in the front line .  You still have Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, you have all these players, Quinyon Mitchell, and Rick Woolen is still around .  Cooper DeJean continues to do his thing .  Zack Baun. There are still a lot of very good players on this Eagles defense, so you would expect them to be pretty good One comment that has been repeated to me throughout the week is that they are a more aggressive version.  It seems they are sending more pressure, or at least pressure schemes. But what has made the Eagles' defense so inconsistent this year relative to their talent level? First, at the beginning of the season, the inconsistent play, losing games at the end like against the Rams, or even against the Titans, whom they let come back into the game at the end. And it was because, at least from my point of view, at the beginning of the season, it was an accumulation of plays because the offense was not staying on the field.   You know, they had the highest three-and-out rate in the NFL, and basically the defense would rack up too many plays and just say they couldn't hold out that long and end up losing in the end. Then the situation changed to that excuse no longer being valid when you're not creating any pressure at all. McCarthy just before the bye week, but before that, he was like Jonathan Gannon, for whom you gave up two third-round picks, a former Pro Bowler, who was signed to a four-year, $100 million contract on draft weekend.
